Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:28: It also divides in a different manner, in two categories: for all the aspects taken from the four elements are called the yesodit (foundational) soul, which divides into the aforementioned faculties, domem, tzomeach, chai, and medaber; and the soul of Vilon is the Keter over all of them and is called the intellective soul (nefesh sichlit); and what comes from the other nine firmaments divides into ruach, neshamah, chayah, and yechidah of the nefesh, and all of them together are called one nefesh of Assiyah, in respect of the totality of the worlds:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:29: And afterward he takes one ruach from the World of Yetzirah, and it too divides into several levels in the manner mentioned above; but in respect of the totality of all the worlds it is called ruach. And in this manner, neshamah from Beriah, chayah from Atzilut, and yechidah from Adam Kadmon:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:30: And thus the nature of man has been well explained, that he includes all the worlds entirely, both in their totality and in their particulars, which is not so with any of the other creatures, higher or lower, for the offspring of any given world include only the world in which they were created.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:31: And this concerns the matter of the worlds from below to above; he also includes all the worlds from within to without. How so? In the World of Assiyah he has a body from the earth, called the lowly world, and within it the yesodit soul from the aspect of the kelipot, and within it, from the aspect of the angels of this world, who were created for all the needs of this world, to cause the growth of plants and so on, and within it, from the aspect of the souls of human beings. And all these become a chariot for the light drawn from the lights of the ten sefirot of Assiyah, which are within the four elements, in order to give them life, and they are innermost of all; and it is the same in this manner regarding what man possesses from the spheres of Assiyah and from the three worlds Yetzirah, Beriah, Atzilut:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:32: And now we have explained all the answers to the questions we wrote at the beginning of this gate. For behold, the light of the quarry of the souls is more inward and higher than the light of the quarry of the angels, and therefore they are its servants, for through it their illumination and vitality is drawn from the light of the ten sefirot to them:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:33: And this is the mystery of (Isaiah 33:7), "behold, their valiant ones cry out outside" — for when abundance is not drawn from the ten sefirot to the souls of Israel, who are inward to them, their own influence, which comes to them, being outward to them, is lacking, so they cried out at the time of the destruction, being outward from the souls. And therefore they did not descend to clothe themselves also in this world in a body, for they would necessarily have been lost through the kelipot, since even the inward souls have no power to withstand the kelipot, how much more so they. And the proof is from the Nefilim, who sought to descend and were lost from the world, and will be blotted out in the future to come. And there is an even greater reason than this: for due to their own deficiency they could not draw down abundance to all the worlds except from their own aspect outward, and even this is impossible, for they themselves do not draw abundance for themselves except through the souls. It is true that the soul in the World of Yetzirah is lesser than the angel in Beriah, and so on in the other worlds; however, the soul in Beriah is greater than the angel of Beriah itself, and so in every world by itself:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:34: The greatness of the soul is also explained: that it is a light born and drawn from the light of the ten sefirot themselves, without any intermediary, and for this they are called (Deuteronomy 14:1), "you are children to the Lord your God," for they are, in their aspect, like a child attached to its father completely, and drawn from him; and this is the mystery of (Bereishit Rabbah 47), "the Patriarchs, they themselves are the Chariot" to the light of the ten sefirot that rides upon them, not through the intermediary of any other light — and this is the mystery of (Isaiah 49:3), "Israel, in whom I shall be glorified," for the garment of a man is his splendor (tiferet), as it is written (ibid. 61:10), "like a bridegroom who acts as a priest with a garland, and like a bride who adorns herself with her jewels":
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:35: Now, the light of the souls is a garment to the light of the ten sefirot, and this is the mystery of (Song of Songs 6:2), "my beloved has gone down to his garden" — this world — "to graze in the gardens and to gather lilies," an acrostic for "garment," for he gathers the souls of the righteous, who give off a fragrance like lilies through their deeds in this world, and gathers them so that His light may clothe itself in them; and this is the mystery of (Deuteronomy 4:4), "and you who cleave to the Lord" — a complete attachment to the light of the ten sefirot, which is not so with any of the other creatures; and this is what is written (Jeremiah 13:11), "for as a loincloth clings to the loins of a man, so have I made the whole house of Israel cling to Me":
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:36: It has also been explained what the matter of the good inclination and the evil inclination within man is: for they are two formations added to man, apart from his soul, and they are: a light from the light of the angels, called the good inclination; and a light from the light of the kelipot, called the evil inclination, which stands outside the good inclination as a kelipah to it,
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:37: but the soul of man itself is the innermost of all, and being innermost, and also since it is called the very essence of the person, therefore he has the power of free choice to incline toward wherever he wishes, for it is greater than they. Nevertheless, its essential inclination is toward the good inclination, since the good inclination is holy like itself, and also since it is closer to it; but the body's essential inclination is toward the evil inclination, since both are on the side of evil and also since they are close to one another. And it is in this respect that the strife between matter and the soul lies, for since the soul performs the commandments only through the body, which inclines more toward the evil inclination, there is great difficulty in subduing them in this respect:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:38: It has thus been explained that in its choice the soul is able to incline toward the good inclination, but since it needs the actions of the body, it has great labor to subdue the evil inclination. And understand all this well: how after death there is no punishment either for the soul or for the body until they are clothed together again as they were in life:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:39: And let us now explain the answer to the first two questions: what need was there for the creation of man with a body, and further, what is the reason two inclinations, good and evil, were formed within him; and let us also explain the meaning of the verses (Psalms 68:35), "ascribe strength to God," (Deuteronomy 32:18) "You neglected the Rock who bore you," and so on:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:40: Behold, at the beginning of Creation, all the worlds were created in the order mentioned above, by the power of the Ein Sof, through simple will, in the manner of a free gift and of kindness; afterward it was still necessary to continue drawing down nourishment, vitality, and abundance into all the worlds, to maintain them in their state as at the time of their creation, and no more, as it is written (Ecclesiastes 3:14), "I know that whatever God does, it shall be forever; nothing can be added to it, and nothing taken from it," and as it is written (ibid. 1:9), "and there is nothing new under the sun," and it is written (Genesis 2:2), "and God finished on the seventh day His work," and so on.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:41: This concerns the matter of Creation itself; however, the continued drawing of their vitality from then on required their own deeds, that they sustain themselves — like a son who, once grown, no longer eats at his father's table. But the ten sefirot themselves do not need man's deeds, for the abundance necessary to maintain them in their state, once they were emanated, is drawn to them continuously from the Ein Sof, for of the ten sefirot it is said (Psalms 5:5), "evil shall not sojourn with You," and they have no need of rectification through deeds — which is not so with the created beings from the aspect of the souls and outward, which are mixed with good and evil and require deeds and rectification.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:42: However, in another respect: when abundance is withheld from the created beings, it appears, God forbid, as weakness and a diminishing of ability in the ten sefirot, that they do not bestow upon them; therefore it is said (Deuteronomy 32:18), "You neglected the Rock who bore you," and conversely (Psalms 68:35), "ascribe strength to God":
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:43: And there is yet another reason: for even if a person is himself healthy and clean, he desires that his garments be splendid in proportion to his own greatness; and so too the sefirot themselves appear, as it were, weak, they themselves, when the created beings are not rectified, and this is [the meaning of] "ascribe strength to God" — "Israel, in whom I shall be glorified," as mentioned above, and thus the third question has been explained:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:44: And so, for the reasons mentioned, it was necessary to create one man who would include all the created and emanated beings, binding together all the worlds as mentioned above, down to the depths of the earth, for he is closest to receiving the abundance from the ten sefirot, and then, through the rectification of his deeds, he draws the abundance from the ten sefirot to himself, and from himself to the angels, and from them to the kelipot, in order to rectify from them whatever can be clarified, as will be explained regarding the evil inclination, and from them to the worlds themselves, which are the vessels and bodies of every single world; and if, God forbid, he sins, he ruins all the worlds,
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:45: and thus has been explained the need for the creation of man in the lowly world with a body and a soul, and with the good inclination and the evil inclination. And there is another reason closely related to this, concerning the matter of the evil inclination: for man is compelled by his own nature to bear children and to eat, and all this necessarily in purity; and he is also compelled, on behalf of every single world, to draw down the abundance that becomes materialized within them, for the sake of the vessels, which are the worlds themselves, and without them, the vessels would not endure, for they are finer than they, and are themselves included among the levels of Creation — understand this well.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:46: It is thus found that it was necessary for man to be composed of all the worlds, so that they would assist him in his deeds to draw down the abundance for himself and for them, for they alone have no power to draw it down. And therefore, when man sins, all the worlds are ruined and receive punishment and a diminishing of abundance in themselves, since they did not assist him — understand this well. And this is the mystery of "all wickedness shall be consumed as smoke," for the kelipot are the cause of sin more than all the rest, and therefore their punishment is great. Indeed, regarding the good that is clarified from them, it is said (Deuteronomy 6:5), "and you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart" — with your two inclinations, for even the evil inclination can be clarified; but the residue within it, which is necessarily evil, of it is said (Psalms 68:3), "as smoke is driven away, so drive them away":
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:47: And thus it has been explained that man is composed of all the worlds, and this is what is written (Ecclesiastes 12:13), "for this is the whole of man," and this is the mystery of (Genesis 1:26), "let us make man in our image, according to our likeness" — and it is written "let us make" in the plural, for all the worlds participated in his making, and thus he includes the image of man within all the worlds, for they all have need of his deeds. And this is the mystery of (Genesis 2:15), "and He placed him in the Garden of Eden to work it and to guard it" — through positive and negative commandments; and as it is written (ibid., v. 5), "for the Lord God had not caused it to rain upon the earth," for the reason that there was no man to work the ground. And this is the mystery of (Isaiah 51:16), "and I have put My words in your mouth... to plant the heavens..." for through his deeds man draws down life to the heavens and the earth, and it is as though he had planted and established them, and thus it is found that "you are with Me," as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (in the introduction to the Zohar, 4b, and in Tikkunei Zohar 69), "a partner with Me: I create, and you sustain":
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:48: And now the matter of prophecy should not seem difficult in your eyes, as our Sages, of blessed memory, said regarding (Deuteronomy 11:22), "and to cleave to Him," (ibid. 10:20) "and to Him shall you cleave" — for the prophet cleaves to the blessed Name through the drawing down of prophecy and abundance to the lower beings, as Nachmanides and all the commentators, of blessed memory, wrote. And this is no wonder, for it has been explained that there is no light attached to the light of the ten sefirot like the light of the quarry of the souls, for this is the mystery of (Deuteronomy 4:4), "and you who cleave to the Lord your God are all alive today":
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 3:1-3: It has been explained in the preceding gate that it is easy for man to prophesy, since he includes all the worlds and all of them are sustained through his deeds. It thus follows from all this that, on the contrary, prophecy is necessarily bound to exist in the world, in order to guide man to rectify his deeds so as to draw down abundance to all the worlds, so that they not be nullified, God forbid, as it is written (Job 33:15), "in a dream, a vision of the night... then He opens the ears of men... to turn man from his deed," and so on. And had prophecy not rested upon Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, and had he not brought down the Torah from heaven, which sustains the worlds, as it is written (Jeremiah 33:25), "if not for My covenant day and night, I would not have set the laws of heaven and earth," the worlds would have been destroyed, God forbid. And in his path all the other prophets followed, to guide the people and to enlighten their eyes in the wisdom of the Torah and its secrets, through the Holy Spirit that clothed itself within them:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 3:4: It follows that prophecy and the Holy Spirit are necessarily bound to exist in the world, and it is an easy matter — but on condition that there be found people fit for it. But when the soul is blemished, it is impossible; therefore let us explain the manner of this obstruction:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 3:5: Behold, when the abundance of the Holy Spirit is stirred to descend upon a person and to rest upon him, and he is a sinner, the evil inclination causes a dark screen between the intellective soul and the source of the Holy Spirit, and this is what is written (Isaiah 59:2), "but your iniquities have separated," and so on, and the Holy Spirit does not rest upon him — and this is through the 365 transgressions that blemish the intellective soul, as mentioned in Part One:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 3:6: Also, if the blemish is due to the lack of some commandment among the 248 positive commandments, he has a blemish and no supernal abundance is drawn to the intellective soul while some limb is damaged and blemished; and indeed if the blemish is lower down, in the yesodit soul, due to bad character traits in the animal soul, or due to forbidden foods that make the vegetative soul detestable, and so on for all such things, then there will be no lower force stirred to draw down the supernal abundance, and a separating screen is made there, and no lower arousal ascends from below to draw down the abundance from above to below:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 3:7: It follows that there are several kinds of screens: whether a screen between the vegetative soul and above, due to a blemish through forbidden foods, whose power is in the vegetative soul; or whether they are due to bad character traits or transgressions that come through desire and the arousal of the animal soul, which blemish it; or whether they are transgressions of speech, coming from the speaking soul; or whether they are in thought and imagination, which blemish the intellective soul. And it has already been explained that all the blemishes affect only that particular spark belonging to that soul, at each level and in each world — understand this. And sometimes, when the blemishes grow strong, this soul's branch is cut off from the trunk of the tree, called the light of the quarry of the souls, through the aforementioned separating screen. And this is the mystery of what our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Berachot 18b), the wicked, in their lifetime, are called dead:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 3:8: It has already been explained that not all blemishes are equal, for there is a blemish that blemishes the vegetative, and one in the animal, and one in the speaking, and one in the intellective. However, regarding the matter of drawing down the Holy Spirit, since there is a blemish in any place whatsoever, it cannot be drawn down at all; therefore whoever comes to purify himself must have all his levels like clear glass, cleansed of all the defilement of the evil inclination mixed into all the levels of the soul. And this is what was said to Moses our teacher, peace be upon him (Exodus 3:5), "remove your shoes from your feet" — meaning that all the limbs of his body and the faculties of his soul, at all its levels mentioned, should be pure, without any dross of turbid matter at all, as mentioned in Sefer HaTikkunim (see Tikkun 12 and Tikkun 21), and that no venom of the evil inclination remain in him at all except for the clarified good portion within it, which is necessary only for the sustenance of the body; and then there is nothing to obstruct or separate between the faculties of the soul and their source in the light of the quarry of the souls, which is attached to the source of the Holy Spirit within the light of the ten sefirot:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 3:9: It has thus been explained that the blemish causes two evils: the first, that the desire and will of the lower being cannot ascend to the source of the Holy Spirit; and secondly, that on account of this, the supernal Holy Spirit likewise cannot extend down to the lower being — and all this is due to the screen of sins mentioned. And indeed, the cause of the blemish necessarily occurs through the shared faculties in the body, [namely] the nefesh of the domem, which are bound with a strong bond to the body itself, for it is the vessel through which the soul acts with all its kinds of faculties. However, not all the faculties of the soul are found in every kind of blemish, for there is a blemish in the vegetative, and one in the animal, and one in the speaking, and one in the intellective, as mentioned above. But the faculties of the domem soul and the faculties of the body are found in every kind of blemish in the world:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 4:1-3: On the conditions for prophecy, in great brevity. It has already been explained that there are blemishes that blemish the vegetative soul, and some in the animal, and some in the speaking, and some in the intellective, and one must purify them all. If so, one must first return in complete repentance from every kind of transgression or bad character trait, and never return to them again. And afterward he should take care to fulfill, as much as possible in this time, all 248 positive commandments, as we explained in Part One, and especially those meant for setting fixed times for Torah study by day and by night — not to omit even a single day — and to pray his three prayers each day with complete intention, and to fulfill Grace after Meals and all the blessings over pleasure with intention, and to honor the Sabbath in all its particulars, and to fulfill "and you shall love your neighbor as yourself" with a whole heart, and to fulfill the recitation of the Shema, and tzitzit, and tefillin in his prayers.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 4:4: Afterward he should take care not to sin at all in any of the 365 negative commandments, even in the fine points of the Rabbinic enactments, and especially in those among all the transgressions liable to karet, and death by the hand of Heaven, and death by the court. And of the other negative commandments he should be careful, and especially of these: gossip-mongering, evil speech, idle talk, mockery, gazing at forbidden sights, every kind of seminal emission, every kind of closeness to a menstruant woman, and an oath even when true; and in the observance of the Sabbath more than anything.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 4:5: And he should be careful of every unseemly character trait, for they defile the yesodit soul, and especially of pride, to the very last degree, until he becomes like the lowest threshold, which everyone treads upon, and lowliness should be truly implanted in his heart, so that he does not feel joy at one who honors him nor shame at one who insults him, and both should be equal in his eyes. And of anger, even if they strike him on his cheeks, for there is nothing that prevents the Holy Spirit more than anger. And of touchiness, to the very last degree, even with his own household. And of sadness, to the very last degree, for prophecy does not rest at all, even upon one fit for it, amid sadness. And he should be glad with his lot even at a time when sufferings come upon him, as it is written (Deuteronomy 6:5), "and you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart," and so on.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 4:6: And after all this, he should occupy himself with all his strength in Torah lishmah, entirely, solely to give satisfaction to his Maker. When he occupies himself with Torah and commandments, he should be joyful to the very last degree, as it is written (Psalms 119:162), "I rejoice at Your word, like one who finds great spoil," for through this he draws down abundance to all the worlds. And the essence of all this is his fear of Him, blessed be He, always, at every moment, so as not to sin, and this is achieved by setting the Name before his eyes, as it is written (Psalms 16:8), "I have set the Lord before me always." And he should intend to fasten his thought upon Him, without ceasing even for a moment, and this is the mystery of "and to cleave to Him," "and to Him shall you cleave":
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 5:1-3: On the quality of prophecy, what its nature is:

Behold, it has been explained that there is one light, in the form of Adam, extending through all four worlds — Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah, Assiyah — down to the end of the four elements of the lowly world, and it attaches itself to the lights of the supernal Adam, called the ten sefirot, and they clothe themselves within this light called the light of the quarry of the souls, and all the souls of the lower beings are included there. And when they descend into this world to clothe themselves in bodies, they leave their roots attached at their source, from which they were hewn, and only the branches of those roots descend, by way of extension alone, and clothe themselves in bodies in this world — like the branches of a tree, which are attached and rooted in the trunk of the tree itself, and bend themselves downward and touch the very ground while still being held fast to the trunk of the tree. And when a person commits a sin liable to karet (excision), that branch is cut off from the trunk of the tree and remains separated from it, existing in this world like the spirit of a beast — and this is the mystery of "that soul shall surely be cut off (hikkaret tikkaret)." And this is the mystery of "for man is a tree of the field":
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 5:4: And this is the mystery of what is written regarding the righteous, that their name is doubled: Abraham, Abraham; Jacob, Jacob; Moses, Moses — one corresponding to the aspect of the root that remains above, attached to the tree, and this is called the person's mazal (constellation/fortune). And as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Menachot 29b), that Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, saw the mazal of Rabbi Akiva sitting and expounding, and so on, for from it the abundance flows to the branch that descended and clothed itself in the body:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 5:5: Now, the root is exceedingly supernal, at the very height of the World of Atzilut, and the branch is exceedingly long, extending through all the worlds until its tip clothes itself in this body; and at every level in every world it leaves there one root, so that there is no soul that does not have roots without end, one above the other, and through his deeds he merits to elevate them all, for all the levels of the World of Assiyah, the roots it left there, are all called together one complete nefesh of Assiyah, and so in the same manner regarding the other levels:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 5:6: And by this the matter of prophecy will be explained: for once a person is refined in matter, without any venom of the evil inclination at all, and not in the faculties of the yesodit soul at all, and he has no sin blemishing any root among the roots of his soul, then, when he prepares himself to attach himself to his supernal root, he can become attached to it. But even though he is fit for this, he must strip his soul entirely and separate it from all matters of matter, and then it can cleave to its spiritual root:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 5:7: Now, this matter of "extension" is not to be understood, as you will find written in all the books concerning matters of prophecy and the Holy Spirit, as an actual physical extension in which the soul literally leaves the body, as in sleep — for if so, this would not be prophecy but merely a dream like all other dreams. Rather, the resting of the Holy Spirit upon a person occurs while the soul is in his body, while he is awake, and it does not leave him.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 5:8: Rather, the matter of this "extension" is that he removes all his thoughts entirely, and the imaginative faculty within him, which is a faculty drawn from the yesodit animal soul within him, ceases to imagine, think, or reflect upon any matter of this world at all, as though his soul had left him; and then he turns the imaginative faculty of his thoughts to imagine and depict as though he were ascending into the supernal worlds, through the roots of his soul which are there, from one to another, until his imagined depiction reaches its supernal source, and the depictions of all the lights become engraved in his thought as though he pictures and sees them, in the manner his imaginative faculty is able to picture in its mind matters of this world, even though he does not see them, as is known in the science of nature.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 5:9: And then he shall think and intend to receive light from the ten sefirot, from that point where the root of his soul is attached; and he shall intend to elevate the ten sefirot as well, one to another, up to the Ein Sof, and draw illumination to them from there down to their end, and as the light descends through him to them, they rejoice in this and shine with that light which he has drawn down to the root of his soul attached to them, according to the portion befitting it.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 5:10: And he shall intend to bring it down, level by level in descent, until that light and abundance reach his own intellective soul in his body, and from there it reaches the animal soul and the imaginative faculty within it, and there those matters become depicted with a physical depiction in his imaginative faculty, and then he shall understand them as though he actually sees them with his own eyes:
